body.statement: The interior class \(\mathcal M^{\circ}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\) equals the union of the strictly positive Rosenbaum--Rubin binary-logistic full-data families whose treatment coefficient obeys \(|\alpha_x|\leq\log\Gamma_A\) and whose outcome coefficients obey \(|\delta_{a,x}|\leq\log\Gamma_a\), with intercepts varying freely subject to the observed margin.  Its closure \(\mathcal M\) is exactly the set of compatible laws in \(\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}\) satisfying the closed joint-cell inequalities in \(\zeta\) and \(\eta\); no conditional odds ratio is evaluated at a null cell.
body.justification: This pins the new bounded class to the published fixed-parameter model rather than introducing an unrelated analogue.
body.gap: Rosenbaum--Rubin specify coefficients tuple by tuple; the bounded union and its probability-table closure are not formulated there.
body.consumer: Readers can translate familiar logistic sensitivity coefficients directly into the sharp identified-set class.
body.proof_tex:
Work first under a law in \(\mathcal M^\circ\).  Strict positivity makes every conditional probability below lie in \((0,1)\).  Define
\[
e_{u,x}=\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=u,X=x),
\qquad
\alpha_x=\operatorname{logit}(e_{1,x})-\operatorname{logit}(e_{0,x}).
\]
Then, with \(b_x=\operatorname{logit}(e_{0,x})\),
\[
\operatorname{logit}\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=u,X=x)=b_x+\alpha_xu.
\]
Cancellation of the positive \(U,X\) margins gives
\[
e^{\alpha_x}
=\frac{\zeta_{1,1,x}\zeta_{0,0,x}}
       {\zeta_{1,0,x}\zeta_{0,1,x}}.
\]
Thus Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}odds\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}odds\text{-}lower}\) hold if and only if \(|\alpha_x|\leq\log\Gamma_A\).

Similarly, latent ignorability from Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}latent\text{-}ignorability}\) permits the arm-specific conditional risks to be written without conditioning on \(A\).  Define
\[
\delta_{a,x}=\operatorname{logit}(\mu_{a,1,x})-
              \operatorname{logit}(\mu_{a,0,x}),
\qquad
c_{a,x}=\operatorname{logit}(\mu_{a,0,x}).
\]
Then
\[
\operatorname{logit}\widetilde P\{Y(a)=1\mid U=u,X=x\}
=c_{a,x}+\delta_{a,x}u,
\]
and cancellation of the positive \(U,X\) margins yields
\[
e^{\delta_{a,x}}
=\frac{\eta_{a,1,1,x}\eta_{a,0,0,x}}
       {\eta_{a,1,0,x}\eta_{a,0,1,x}}.
\]
The two outcome inequalities are therefore equivalent to \(|\delta_{a,x}|\leq\log\Gamma_a\).  The intercepts \(b_x,c_{a,x}\) remain unrestricted except for the observed-margin equations.  This proves both inclusions between \(\mathcal M^\circ\) and the stated union of positive binary-logistic families.

For completeness, consider the closure claim in probability-table coordinates.  Observed-margin compatibility is affine; consistency is imposed by the deterministic map \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\); latent ignorability is the collection of finite-table cross-product equalities; and all four odds restrictions are the displayed weak polynomial inequalities.  Their common solution set \(C\subset\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}\) is closed.  Hence \(\mathcal M\subseteq C\).

For the reverse inclusion, take a table in \(C\).  In each stratum its treatment-confounder table is represented by its posterior pair \((w_0,w_1)\in D_{A,x}\).  For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), set
\[
w_a^{(\varepsilon)}=(1-\varepsilon)w_a+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}.
\]
The map \(T_\varepsilon(v)=(1-\varepsilon)v+\varepsilon/2\) contracts log-odds differences, because
\[
T_\varepsilon(v)\{1-T_\varepsilon(v)\}
\geq(1-\varepsilon)v(1-v),
\qquad
\left|\frac{d\operatorname{logit}T_\varepsilon(v)}
{d\operatorname{logit}v}\right|\leq1.
\]
Thus \((w_0^{(\varepsilon)},w_1^{(\varepsilon)})\in D_{A,x}\cap(0,1)^2\) and it converges to the original pair.  Choose bounded log-odds differences \(\delta_{a,x}^{(\varepsilon)}\in[-\log\Gamma_a,\log\Gamma_a]\) converging to each identified limiting difference; where a latent cell is null, choose any convergent value because that conditional margin carries vanishing mass.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) supplies the unique intercept which preserves exactly the observed risk \(r_{a,x}\).  The resulting conditional risks are in \((0,1)\) and their probability tables converge to the original nonnull margins.  Finally, every binary coupling of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) with given marginals is indexed by its \((1,1)\)-cell in the closed Fréchet interval; choosing an interior point of the corresponding perturbed interval and letting it converge to the original cell produces strictly positive conditional joint tables.  Use the same conditional coupling for both treatment values.  This preserves latent ignorability, while Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}observed\text{-}margin}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\) preserve the observed law.  These positive tables belong to \(\mathcal M^\circ\) and converge to the given table.  Hence \(C\subseteq\mathcal M\), proving the asserted closed-table characterization without evaluating an odds ratio at a null cell.
